newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-SPANISH LEAGUE MATCHES THIS WEEKEND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SPANISH LEAGUE MATCHES THIS WEEKEND.

text.p: Spanish championship matches this weekend (kickoff times GMT, league standings in parentheses):
Russian midfielder Valery Karpin returns to his old club in a Valencia side rocked by their midweek cup exit to second division Las Palmas. Striker Claudio Lopez on duty with Argentina.
Atletico won 3-2 in midweek cup action between the two sides, but the champions without Daniel Prodan, who was sent off in the game. Compostela keeper Fernando Peralta out with ankle injury.

Argentine coach Carlos Bilardo returned to Sevilla midweek and makes his debut in a game between two big clubs in desperate need of a result. Zaragoza must wait for a late appeal against suspension of forward Gustavo Poyet.
Racing knocked Athletic Bilbao out of the cup and will be looking to end some erratic home form against a Sporting side that has recovered in recent games.
Oviedo will be without injured midfielders Peter Dubovsky and Ivan Iglesias, but have match-winner in Oli Alvarez in their bid to turn around last season's sensational 8-3 defeat in the fixture.
A last-minute goal saved Rayo's cup bid -- and with it the job of manager Paquito Gomez -- but the Madrid side badly need to halt a run of league defeats.

High-flying Betis showed they can win at home as well as away by beating Tenerife 3-0 in the cup. They hope to repeat the 3-0 win of earlier in the season against an Extremadura side that is playing with renewed spirt.
Real without key defender Fernando Hierro, sent off in the cup elimination by Barcelona. Fernando Sanzz the most likely replacement.

With FIFA disciplinary action and a cup exit, Deportivo desperately need a win in the Galician derby with rivals Celta, who are without Brazilian midfielder Mazinho and coach Fernando Santos, both suspended.
Struggling Logrones missing Uruguayan defender Ricardo Canals, who has influenza. Tenerife crashed out of the cup and lost midfielder Ignacio Conte through injury in the process.
Espanyol hope to win an appeal against the suspension of goalkeeper Pascal Olmeta for a Catalan derby in which Barcelona will be boosted by the cup win over Real Madrid.
